newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Edrasi sees 96 profit down 16.6pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek Edrasi sees 96 profit down 16.6pct.

text.p: Construction firm Edrasi Psallidas expects its 1996 pre-tax profit to fall 16.6 percent to 1.25 billion drachmas from 1.50 billion in 1995, company officials told institutional investors.
Turnover is estimated at 6.8 billion drachmas for 1996, up 7.0 percent on 1995. It is expected to rise 10.2 percent in 1997 to 7.5 billion drachmas.
Edrasi had an orderbook of yet uncompleted projects worth 13 billion drachmas in January.
In 1995, it established Edrafor S.A.L. in Lebanon, specialising in geotechnical works, where it has a 50 percent stake.
Edrafor is among the four biggest international companies that undertake similar projects in Lebanon. In 1997, Edrafor's turnover is estimated around five million dollars.
Edrasi also cooperates with Alte and TEB in joint projects in Balkan and eastern European countries. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
